verdicts.tldr: a fork's realm directory name reaches the bot comment unescaped, so it can introduce markup into a comment the repository's own token posts
verdicts.details: Confirmed by read and by my own run. Realm paths are the fork's directory names: plan.go:136-141 sets Pkg.Path from the walked directory and never reads the gnomod module line, so nothing validates them. comment.go then writes that string raw into markdown code spans (33, 63, 80, 154) and into HTML attributes (112, 118, 121), and pr-preview-publish.yml:174/177 posts the resulting file verbatim as github-actions[bot] under the repository token. Two limits I measured that the candidate does not state. First, the finder's own payload is not deliverable: pr-preview.yml's `git diff --name-only` is the only source of the changed-file list, and git quotes a path containing `"` (`"examples/gno.land/r/ev\"il/lib.gno"`), so the alt= breakout it demonstrated never reaches BuildPlan; a backtick is passed through unquoted and closes the code span instead, which is the deliverable form. Second, the render must still finish: plan.Dirs hands the hostile directory to gnodev, and waitReady (crawl.go:589) needs HTTP 200 on Realms[0], so the attack wants a second, ordinary realm sorting first — a link I read but did not boot. Fix: escape every realm and package path before it is written, `html.EscapeString` for the attribute forms and a backtick-and-bracket escape for the markdown ones, or drop any path outside `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+` from the comment.
verdicts.evidence: Head ecf7af0f2, misc/gnopreview. Finder's artifact rerun from the file: `go test -run TestB5CommentEscapesRealmNames -v .` FAILs with `alt="x">">`. My own check, tests/judge-83-realm-name-deliverable-by-git_test.go: TestJudge83QuoteIsNotDeliverable PASSes (git reports [] — the quoted path is dropped), TestJudge83BacktickBreaksTheCodeSpan FAILs with ChangedRealms=["gno.land/r/aaa" "gno.land/r/zz``y"] and the emitted line `- [`gno.land/r/zz``y`](https://example.test/pr-1/r/zz``y/)`. gnomod/file.go:122 `module.CheckImportPath` rejects such a module path, which is why the payload rides the directory name.

verdicts.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestCatalogEmptyPlanCanClearTheComment -v . ; grep -n "skip != " .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml ; grep -n "continue-on-error|outcome == |no comment body" .github/workflows/pr-preview-publish.yml
verdicts.tldr: a push that reverts the last realm change leaves the previous comment standing, so the PR shows screenshots and links of an older head
verdicts.details: Confirmed by rerunning the artifact and by reading all three workflows. Comment returns "" for a plan with nothing to preview (comment.go:24-26), and no path on the publish side ever removes or rewrites the comment for that case: pr-preview.yml gates the gnodev build, the render and actions/upload-artifact on `if: steps.plan.outputs.skip != 'true'` (lines 85, 92, 118), so no artifact exists; pr-preview-publish.yml downloads with `continue-on-error: true` (54) and gates every later step on `steps.download.outcome == 'success'` (68), so the job is green and silent; and the upsert step exits 0 on `[ -s _preview/comment.md ]` (166) before reaching the only two writes, the PATCH at 174 and the POST at 177. The one deletion is pr-preview-cleanup.yml on `pull_request_target: closed`, so the stale body survives every further push until the PR closes. What the reader loses is the signal, not the preview: the comment keeps saying "Rebuilt on every push to this PR" while linking snapshots of a head that no longer exists. Fix: make Comment emit the marker and a one-line "nothing to preview on this head" body for an empty plan, and let the skip branch upload that artifact so the upsert replaces the old comment.

verdicts.tldr: the switch promises per-mode branches that do not exist, and a fifth mode would land silently in its default
verdicts.details: Confirmed by read and by applying the rewrite. Mode() (plan.go:94-103) returns four strings; Comment's Empty() guard at comment.go:24 removes "none" exactly, since Empty() is the same predicate, so the default is reached by "both" and "realms" alone and its first statement re-reads p.Gnoweb to separate them — one fact read through two sources. The saving is shape, not size: 196 -> 195 lines in the file, 48 -> 47 in the Comment body. Nothing observable changes, which is why this is the author's call and not a defect. Fix: `if p.Mode() == "gnoweb" { ... } else { ... }`, or keep the switch and give "both" and "realms" their own cases so a later mode cannot land in a default that was never written for it.
verdicts.evidence: Rewrite applied in a scratch worktree at ecf7af0f2: `gofmt -l .` silent, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` -> `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/misc/gnopreview 0.005s` with the finder's tests/b5-refactor-comment-golden_test.go copied in.
